source: marineregions.org gazetteer search API (https://www.marineregions.org/rest/getGazetteerRecordsByName.json/, tokenless, confirmed live during ticket 0.8 scoping)
note: Polygon vertices are rectangular bounding boxes from real, cited sources, not hand-drawn guesses -- an improvement in provenance over the fully-invented boxes these replace. They are NOT precise legal reserve boundaries (real reserves are irregular polygons, and in the Bonifacio case cover more area than the archipelago's own extent) -- see each zone's 'precise_boundary_verified' and 'caveat'. Follow-up: EEA's own Natura2000 WFS or French INPN open data for the actual designated-area polygons (ticket 0.8 plan, 'Real-data sourcing').

zones.name: Reserve de Scandola
zones.gazetteer_name: Gulf of Porto: Calanche of Piana, Gulf of Girolata, Scandola Reserve
zones.caveat: Real, cited bounding box (UNESCO World Heritage Marine Programme via marineregions.org) -- still a rectangular approximation of an irregular real reserve boundary, not the legal designation polygon itself.

zones.name: Iles Lavezzi archipelago
zones.caveat: Real, cited bounding box for the archipelago itself (marineregions.org) -- the actual Reserve naturelle des Bouches de Bonifacio marine reserve extends well beyond this to cover much of the strait's southern Corsican waters; this box is deliberately the tighter, precisely-sourced archipelago extent rather than a guessed wider reserve boundary. The physical islets themselves are already represented precisely by the real GSHHG coastline data (core.geography.RealGeography) independent of this no-go zone.
